content.user_title: Build Better Claude Code Plugin Skills
content.value_statement: Authoring effective Claude Code plugin skills requires knowing the right structure, metadata, and progressive disclosure patterns. This skill provides step-by-step guidance so you can create well-organized skills that load the right context at the right time.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md structure and YAML frontmatter fields.
Guides a six-step skill creation process from examples to iteration.
Describes progressive disclosure across metadata, SKILL.md body, and bundled resources.
Provides writing-style rules such as imperative form and third-person descriptions.
Includes a validation checklist and a list of common mistakes to avoid.
Shows how to organize scripts, references, examples, and assets in a plugin skill.
limitations: Provides guidance only; it does not generate or install skills automatically.
Focuses on Claude Code plugin skills, not other plugin components.
Does not validate or execute any scripts you write.
Assumes familiarity with basic Markdown and YAML syntax.

use_cases.title: Create a new plugin skill
use_cases.description: A developer builds a new skill for a Claude Code plugin using the recommended structure and process.

use_cases.title: Improve an existing skill description
use_cases.description: A maintainer rewrites a weak skill description to include specific trigger phrases and third-person format.

use_cases.title: Organize skill content with progressive disclosure
use_cases.description: A technical writer moves detailed content into reference files to keep SKILL.md lean and focused.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for my plugin that helps format JSON files. Use the recommended structure.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a skill description
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve the description of my skill so it triggers on the right user queries. Use third-person format and specific trigger phrases.

prompt_templates.title: Reorganize with progressive disclosure
prompt_templates.prompt: My SKILL.md is over 5000 words. Reorganize it using progressive disclosure and move detailed content into reference files.

prompt_templates.title: Design a complete skill with resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a complete skill for building frontend web apps, including which scripts, references, and assets to bundle and why.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for rotating PDF files.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a directory with a SKILL.md file, a scripts folder holding a rotate_pdf script, and frontmatter with a third-person description and clear trigger phrases such as rotate this PDF.

output_examples.input: My skill description is too vague. How do I fix it?
output_examples.output: The skill recommends rewriting the description in third person, listing exact phrases users would say, and naming concrete scenarios so Claude Code triggers the skill reliably.

best_practices: Write descriptions in third person with specific trigger phrases users would actually say.
Keep SKILL.md lean, around 1,500 to 2,000 words, and move detailed content to reference files.
Use imperative, verb-first instructions throughout the skill body.
anti_patterns: Putting all content in a single large SKILL.md file instead of using reference files.
Writing vague descriptions without concrete trigger phrases.
Using second-person language such as you should instead of direct imperative instructions.

faq.question: What files does a skill require?
faq.answer: A skill requires one SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter containing a name and a description. All other resources are optional.

faq.question: How long should SKILL.md be?
faq.answer: Aim for 1,500 to 2,000 words in the body, and keep it under 5,000 words. Move longer content into reference files.

faq.question: What is progressive disclosure?
faq.answer: It is a three-level loading system. Metadata is always in context, the SKILL.md body loads when the skill triggers, and bundled resources load only as needed.

faq.question: How does Claude Code decide when to use a skill?
faq.answer: Claude Code reads the name and description in the frontmatter. Clear trigger phrases and a specific description help it choose the skill at the right time.

faq.question: Do I need to package a plugin skill?
faq.answer: No. Plugin skills are distributed as part of the plugin. Users receive the skill when they install the plugin.

faq.question: Where should scripts and reference files live?
faq.answer: Place executable code in a scripts folder, documentation in a references folder, and output resources in an assets folder within the skill directory.
